verdict.line: You lose the ranged poke war before level 6 but win every trade where you land Thundering Smash's stun, so the lane swings on whether you can force that window.

brief.thesis: Gnar's Boomerang Throw (1100 range) and Hop let him poke and reposition well outside Thundering Smash's 300 range, while Volibear's only ranged tool, Sky Splitter, sits on a 16s cooldown and can't reliably tag a kiting target. The 45.6% head-to-head win rate over 1610 games reflects that structural gap, not a skill deficit — the matchup is decided by forcing trades when Gnar's Hop is down, not by out-poking him.

theirWindow.when: Gnar's Q and E both available
theirWindow.what: He will land free Boomerang Throw damage and threaten to Hop away from any approach. Don't walk up for trades here — you'll eat ranged damage and whiff Thundering Smash at 300 range for nothing.

yourWindow.when: Gnar just used Hop (E) to farm or reposition
yourWindow.what: Close the distance immediately and land Thundering Smash — his only escape is down for 22 to 12 seconds depending on rank, so the stun will land clean.

start.why: The regen and damage reduction on autos directly negate Gnar's chip poke from Boomerang Throw and hyper-charged autos while you wait for a stun window.

boots.why: Gnar's attacks hype his W and chip you down over the laning phase; the flat auto-attack reduction cuts that harassment more than movement speed does here.

core.why: Its slow-and-damage active is your best tool for catching a kiting Mini Gnar when Thundering Smash is on cooldown, and the sustain keeps you in poke wars.
The proc damage and movement speed help you close gaps faster and punish him once he's forced into melee range.
Alternating tenacity blunts his Boomerang Throw and Mega W slows/stuns, letting your stun-chain combo actually connect through his kit.

situational.when: you want cooldown refresh on Q and W to keep stun uptime high through a long lane
gnar out-autos you with hyper stacks and you need the healing cut and reflect damage to punish it
the enemy team adds burst mages or executes that threaten you beyond gnar's own damage

runes.keystoneWhy: The ramping attack speed rewards sticking on Gnar once Thundering Smash lands, letting your Frenzied Maul recast combo and autos outpace his burst before he can reset distance.

summoners.why: Flash and Ignite is the most-run pair (59.7% of games) and closes out kills once you land a Thundering Smash stun on a squishy Gnar; Exhaust+Flash is a strong alternative if you need to shut down Mega Gnar's W stun and mobility in all-ins.

playing.title: Hug minions before level 3
playing.detail: Stand behind your wave so Boomerang Throw and his autos have to go through minions first; Thundering Smash's 300 range means you're already losing if you're poked while approaching.

playing.title: Track Hop, not just Boomerang
playing.detail: Gnar's Hop (E, 22 down to 12s cooldown by rank) is his only escape. Once he uses it to reposition or farm, that's your real window to walk up.

playing.title: Bait Boomerang before closing
playing.detail: Let him throw Q once and miss the catch if possible — losing the catch denies his cooldown refund and buys you several seconds to engage safely.

playing.title: Chain Q into double W
playing.detail: Thundering Smash's stun is your only reliable lock on Mini Gnar. Follow immediately with two Frenzied Maul casts on the same target for the bonus damage and the heal.

playing.title: Respect Mega Gnar's slam
playing.detail: Once his Rage bar maxes and he transforms, his W becomes an area stun instead of a speed buff — don't walk into it blind, or your own stun chain gets interrupted.

playing.title: Poke with Sky Splitter on cooldown
playing.detail: Sky Splitter (16s cooldown, 1200 range) is your only ranged answer. Throw it whenever it's up while he kites, so you're not ceding the entire trading phase to his Boomerang Throw.

playing.title: Save Stormbringer for the chase
playing.detail: Stormbringer's leap is the one tool that catches a fleeing Mini Gnar outside Thundering Smash range — hold it for when he thinks he's safe rather than opening a fight with it.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner picks above come from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1) via OP.GG; the matchup reasoning, timings, and trade patterns are my own read of the kit interactions, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being kited by Mini Gnar by keeping your distance while using [E] to contest lane. Close to fight him once (E) is on cooldown to gain lane control.
